why: Everything is in e2e/ and docs: two stand-in accounts, a measuring spec and a baseline written from a measured run. No production code path changes, and the auth stand-in is the test fake. The weak point is a brief error: the server's HTML always says <html lang="en"> (src/app/admin/layout.tsx:34; the language is set by a script after load). So commit 2's assertion on the fetched document fails and trips the brief's own stop_if, instead of tempting an edit to src.
harm_if_wrong: A flaky or too-loose budget in CI's signed-in job. That can hold up migration deploys until reverted, but it changes nothing users see.
brief_problems: Commit 2 says the nb tests 'expect html to contain <html lang="nb"' on the document fetched with context.request.get. The admin root layout always renders lang="en" (src/app/admin/layout.tsx:34), and adminLangScript()/admin-text.tsx set it in the browser, so that assertion can never pass. Check it in a page with page.locator('html') instead, as commit 1's setup does.
Commit 3 tells the executor to edit a table 'Every budget' in docs/rules/budgets.md that step 1.1 writes, without giving its columns.
